blocks.text: As printed: If \(z_1 = 2 + 7i\) and \(z_2 = -5 + 3i\), the evaluate the following:

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints "the evaluate the following". It should read "then evaluate the following". The question itself is not affected.

blocks.explanation: We need a modulus. The formula \(|a + ib| = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\) works only on a single number \(a + ib\), so first combine the expression into one complex number, then take its modulus and simplify the root.
steps:
Step 3: Simplify the root
\[\sqrt{580} = \sqrt{4 \times 145}\]
\[= 2\sqrt{145}\]
Why: 580 = 4 x 145 and 145 = 5 x 29 has no square factor.

blocks.explanation: Same idea; here we also need the conjugate \(\overline{z_1} = 2 - 7i\).
steps:
Step 1: Work out \(3z_1 + 2\overline{z_1}\)
\[3(2 + 7i) + 2(2 - 7i)\]
\[= 6 + 21i + 4 - 14i\]
\[= 10 + 7i\]
Why: Open the brackets and collect real parts and \(i\) parts.

Step 2: Take the modulus
\[|10 + 7i| = \sqrt{10^{2} + 7^{2}}\]
\[= \sqrt{100 + 49} = \sqrt{149}\]
Why: 149 is prime, so the root cannot be simplified.

Check:
\(\sqrt{149} \approx 12.2\), a little more than 10 and 7: sensible for the length of the vector \(10 + 7i\).

blocks.explanation: Same idea with \(z_2\) and its conjugate \(\overline{z_2} = -5 - 3i\).
steps:
Check:
Common mistake: taking \(b = -27\) and writing \(-27^2 = -729\). The square of the whole \(-27\) is \(+729\).

blocks.explanation: We need the modulus of a cube. Instead of expanding the cube, use \(|z^n| = |z|^n\) (it follows from \(|z_1 z_2| = |z_1||z_2|\)). So find \(z_1 + z_2\), its modulus, and cube it.
steps:
Step 1: Add \(z_1\) and \(z_2\)
\[(2 + 7i) + (-5 + 3i)\]
\[= -3 + 10i\]
Why: Add real parts and imaginary parts separately.

Step 4: Cube it
\[(\sqrt{109})^{3} = \sqrt{109} \cdot \sqrt{109} \cdot \sqrt{109}\]
\[= 109\sqrt{109}\]
Why: Two roots multiply to 109; one root is left.
